messages:
From: Mike Harper <mike@clearskyanalytics.com>

Cc: laura@clearskyanalytics.com
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: High error-rate / latency spike this morning — urgent

Jonas,

We experienced a major spike in latency and 5xx errors on our inference routes this morning starting ~08:45 PST. Traffic pattern was normal on our side; requests started timing out and some batches returned 502/504 repeatedly for ~25 minutes. This impacted critical user flows for 13% of requests (we measured).

Our SRE flagged this as a Sev2 and asked for updates from Redwood. We need a post-incident explanation and confirmation of mitigation steps — our SLAs are sensitive here. Can you share an ETA for an RCA and whether there's an ongoing mitigation to prevent recurrence?

We are looping procurement too; if there are billing/credit implications we need clarity.

Thanks,
Mike Harper
Head of Platform Operations
ClearSky Analytics

Attachments: screenshot_08_50.png (PNG, 200KB)
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 09:35:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: High error-rate / latency spike this morning — urgent

Team — forwarding the ClearSky report. Initial observations from infra: we saw anomalous queue growth on the shared batching nodes serving the model family they use (g7x-enc-llm-v2). KV cache misses spiked and several GPU workers OOMed then were restarted by orchestration, which amplified tail latency.

Immediate asks:
- Marissa: can you own the customer comms and provide a brief interim status update?
- Ben: run the full timeline and log pull (timeline_event_log_20270210-15.csv). Prioritize the batching/logs for 08:30–09:30 PST.
- Neha: check if the routing policy routed traffic to a lower-capacity region during that window.

I’ll start drafting an RCA and propose an exec readout. We should be explicit about compensatory credits and the technical mitigations.

Jonas
Staff PM, Accounts (Redwood)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: High error-rate / latency spike this morning — urgent

Mike — thanks for the heads up and the screenshots. We’re actively investigating and I wanted to confirm we’ve escalated to our infra on-call and are pulling correlated traces. Short answers: we have removed the offending batching pool from rotation and scaled extra capacity to ClearSky’s reservation to stop immediate impact.

Next steps we’ll share by EOD: interim timeline, what triggered the OOMs, and a proposed mitigation plan. Jonas is coordinating an RCA delivery and an executive readout for stakeholders if you’d like to invite your leadership.

Apologies for the hit this morning — we understand the impact.

Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: High error-rate / latency spike this morning — urgent

Logs pulled and preliminary timeline attached (timeline_event_log_20270210-15.csv). Root chain looks like:
- 08:41: spotty memory pressure on batching node pool bpool-17
- 08:44: KV cache miss ratio jumps 4x for the model signature used by ClearSky
- 08:46: two workers report OOM and restart (killed by OOM killer)
- 08:46–09:07: orchestrator auto-restarts cause repeated cold start overhead, spikes in latency 1–5s and a subset of 502/504 responses
- 09:08: bpool-17 evicted from rotation; requests shifted to reserve capacity; latency normalizes by 09:12

Initial root cause hypothesis: insufficient memory headroom on that particular batching configuration combined with a model input variance that increased KV cache churn. There’s also a scheduling policy that allowed low-priority burst neighbors that reduced available headroom.

I recommend these corrective steps:
1) Immediate: blacklist bpool-17; provision temporary reserved nodes for ClearSky (done)
2) Medium: adjust default batching memory target for g7x-enc-llm-v2 and add guardrails for OOM thresholds
3) Long: tooling to detect KV cache churn patterns and proactively shift traffic before restarts

I’ll include a runtime_trace_excerpt.log with the task-level failure markers in the RCA.

—Ben
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Mike Harper <mike@clearskyanalytics.com>, laura@clearskyanalytics.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 16:17:00 -0800
Subject: ClearSky post-incident RCA and proposed corrective plan (attached)

Mike / Laura — attached is our post-incident RCA (clearsky_rca_20270215.pdf) and the collected timeline/log excerpts. High level summary:

- Impact: 25 minutes of elevated latency and a 4.8% increase in 5xx rate across ClearSky’s production routes; peak user impact window 08:46–09:11 PST.
- Primary cause: batching-pool memory pressure + KV cache churn for the g7x-enc-llm-v2 signature + noisy neighbor scheduling allowed low-priority jobs to consume headroom.
- Immediate mitigation completed 10 Feb: bpool-17 removed, temporary reserved nodes provisioned and requests rebalanced.
- Medium-term mitigations (2–4 weeks): adjust batching memory targets, introduce OOM guardrails, add an adaptive routing rule for high cache-churn signatures.
- Long-term (8–12 weeks): telemetry to detect cache-churn patterns, automated preemptive scaling policies, and a hard limit on colocated low-priority bursts for reservation-backed customers.

We propose the following customer-facing commitments:
1) Technical: implement the medium-term mitigations with prioritized test plan and staging validation; target completion 2027-03-05.
2) Operational: a joint post-mortem readout with ClearSky execs — proposed slot Tue 2027-02-16 11:00 PST (30 min). Please confirm availability.
3) Commercial: Redwood will apply a pro-rata credit for the 25-minute impact window under RD-4721 and coordinate with procurement.

Attachments: clearsky_rca_20270215.pdf, timeline_event_log_20270210-15.csv, runtime_trace_excerpt.log

Happy to jump on a call to walk through the RCA line-by-line.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Staff PM, Accounts (Redwood)

- Can you confirm the test plan for the batching memory adjustment includes a staged rollout and perf validation against our 99th percentile latency curve?
- Procurement copied here; please send the credit calculation so we can reconcile.

We’ll take the proposed 02/16 11:00 PST slot for the exec readout — Laura and I will join. Thanks again for the quick response and concrete corrective actions.

Mike

ClearSky Analytics
